item.text:
The change raises IndexError for missing users instead of returning None, as confirmed by execution. It also removes the lookup's early exit, introducing unnecessary traversal and allocation.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Return None when no user matches — /scratch/repo/stats.py:18-18
  When `users` is empty or the requested name is absent, `matches[0]` raises `IndexError` instead of returning `None`. This breaks both the previous behavior and the documented contract. Handle the empty-match case before indexing.

- [P2] Stop scanning after the first matching user — /scratch/repo/stats.py:17-17
  For large collections with an early match, this comprehension scans every user and stores every match even though only the first is returned. The previous implementation returned immediately, so a first-element match now takes linear rather than constant time and can allocate a list proportional to the input size. Preserve the short-circuit lookup.
